subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: What exact authorization, retention, and disclosure contract should let a Slack DM turn recall the agent’s own outbound channel messages?
rationale: The current opt-in agent-wide visibility is broader than the requested behavior, while the default sibling-session isolation is intentional; code cannot safely choose the permanent privacy boundary.

options.title: Scoped self-activity view
options.body: Expose only self-authored outbound Slack activity through a separately authorized agent-scoped query with workspace, account, destination, thread, edit, and deletion boundaries.

options.title: Document agent-wide visibility
options.body: Treat tools.sessions.visibility=agent as the supported solution, accepting that the caller can inspect full same-agent sibling-session history.

options.title: Preserve strict isolation
options.body: Keep the existing boundary and document that DM sessions cannot recall activity from sibling Slack conversations.

recommendation.title: Scoped self-activity view
recommendation.body: Expose only self-authored outbound Slack activity through a separately authorized agent-scoped query with workspace, account, destination, thread, edit, and deletion boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent routing/outbound history and public review place this person closest to the cross-session product and security boundary.
